title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from this page and its neighbours. This is part of the 'suite' of La Longue Marche (pp. 650 bis–787), in which Grothendieck studies the modular group G0 = GL(2,Z) (the next page names it). That group is generated by elements ρ of order 3, σ of order 2 and τ = −id, all acting on a rank-2 lattice M spanned by λ0, λ1 (presumably with λ0+λ1+λ2 = 0, ρ permuting the λi cyclically). He turns the set of 1-cocycles (crossed homomorphisms, i.e. data defining extensions or liftings) of this group with values in M into a scheme Z̃_{ρ,σ} over a base S (S0 being a localization of Spec Z; from the next page, 3 is a point of S0).

A point of Z̃_{ρ,σ} is a triple (μ, α0, β0):
- μ = (ν2, ν3, ν0) is a discrete or 'root-of-unity' parameter, mapping to a scheme O_12^*, plausibly built from the 12 in 12 = 2·2·3 for the abelianization of SL2(Z).
- α0, β0 are sections of the vector group M (Spec Sym M^∨).

On the previous page he introduces the index-3 sublattice M0 = {c0λ0 + c1λ1 : c0 + c1 ≡ 0 (3)}. He notes that the cocycle relation (96) can be rewritten as an equation with values in M0, using the map (α0, β0, ν'') ↦ (1−ρ)(α0 ± ν''(λ1−λ0)) + (1−σ)(β0). Since 1−ρ and 1−σ take values in M0, this is a stricter condition.

This page:
- (104) defines N_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Z̃_{ρ,σ} as the closed subscheme where the cocycle equation is solvable in M0 (a 'stricter' cocycle condition).
- He considers the projection N_{ρ,σ} → O_12^* and states that it is an epimorphism. The fibre over μ is the set of (α0, β0) such that (α̃0, β0) satisfies the linear equation (105): (1−ρ_M)(α̃0) − (1−σ_M)(β0) = 0 in M0.
- (106): the corresponding homomorphism of vector group schemes M × M → M0 is a smooth epimorphism. The reason is that it comes from a surjective Z-linear map of lattices M ⊕ M → M0; indeed 1−ρ alone, of determinant 3, maps M onto M0. Its kernel is therefore a vector group of rank 2, and the fibres are translates of it.
- Conclusion: N_{ρ,σ} is smooth over S0.
- The argument continues on the next page: N is a closed subscheme of Z_{ρ,σ} that coincides with it away from the prime 3. Being flat (smooth), it is the schematic closure of Z_{ρ,σ}|_{Spec Z∖{3}}, and hence a subgroup scheme.

In short, he is constructing a smooth integral model of the cocycle group, correcting the bad (non-flat) behaviour at the prime 3 caused by the order-3 element ρ.

The marginal NB conjectures that N_{ρ,σ} should also be denoted M_{ρ,σ}[0] and realized as (M^♮_{ρ,σ}/M_{ρ,σ})[0], via the relations of §§49–50 of the Longue Marche. That is, it should be a torsion or kernel subgroup of a quotient of a 'saturated' or extended module by the original.
errors: Sign inconsistency: (100)/(101) on the previous page write '+ (1−σ)(β0)', while (105)/(106) here write '− (1−σ)(β0)'. This is harmless for the smoothness argument, since only surjectivity matters.

Smoothness of N over S0 is asserted from fibrewise data: the fibres over O_12^* are translates of a smooth vector group. For this to give smoothness over S0 one needs O_12^* smooth over S0 and N to be (locally) a torsor under the kernel vector group over O_12^*. This is plausible but not spelled out.
'Il est clair que ce morphisme est un épi' needs that the linear equation always has a solution (true since 1−ρ is onto M0), but the dependence of α̃0 on ν'' is passed over.

ideas.what: Scheme of 1-cocycles of the modular group (generated by order-3 and order-2 elements) with coefficients in a lattice, viewed as a group scheme over Spec Z, with a modified 'stricter' cocycle condition valued in an index-3 sublattice M0
ideas.modern_name: Integral model / group scheme of crossed homomorphisms; integral structure on H^1(SL2(Z), M)
ideas.usually_credited_to: general technique (vector group schemes of cocycles); no specific attribution known

ideas.what: A surjection of lattices induces a smooth epimorphism of vector group schemes with smooth kernel
ideas.modern_name: Vector group scheme V(M); exactness of M ↦ V(M) on free modules

ideas.what: Replacing a non-flat closed subgroup scheme by the schematic closure of its generic part to get a flat (smooth) subgroup scheme
ideas.modern_name: Schematic closure / flat closure of a subgroup scheme

missed.claim: The marginal conjecture identifying the smooth model N_{ρ,σ} with M_{ρ,σ}[0] = (M^♮_{ρ,σ}/M_{ρ,σ})[0], tied to §§49–50, is left unverified.
missed.quote: Le groupe N_{ρ,σ} devrait pouvoir se noter aussi M_{ρ,σ}[0], il devrait sauf erreur se réaliser en (M^♮_{ρ,σ}/M_{ρ,σ})[0]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would be an arithmetic (over Spec Z) structure on the cohomology of the modular group with lattice coefficients, with the special behaviour at 3 (and 2) encoded schematically. It is a minor, technical thread, and its meaning depends on §§49–50.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical verification (smoothness via a surjective lattice map, then schematic closure) inside an unpublished, rather idiosyncratic scheme-theoretic treatment of cocycles of GL(2,Z). The overall programme is little known, but this page holds no striking standalone result.
transcription_corrections: (104): the image appears to read 'N_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Z̃_{ρ,σ}' (inclusion, with a crossed-out Z), with '||' below introducing the defining set, rather than 'N = Z̃'.
In the set definition, the crossed-out word seems to be 'cocycles' with a word written above (read as 'locaux'?). The intended reading is probably 'l'équation des cocycles (96) soluble dans M_0'.
The NB ends with 'en vertu des relations des §§ 49, 50' (approximate).
